About Daddy Hunger

From Daddy Hunger to a New Legacy of Fatherhood

Helping fathers heal, grow, reconnect, and create a healthier legacy for their children.

On this pageThe BeginningOur MissionAbout RayThe JourneyThe BookFive PromisesThe VisionInvite Ray

Daddy Hunger began with a simple but painful truth: many children grow up longing for the presence, protection, affirmation, and love of a father.

For Ray Upchurch, that truth was personal.

Ray grew up without knowing his biological father. Years later, after becoming a father himself, he began to understand how deeply a father’s presence—or absence—can shape a child’s identity, emotional safety, relationships, and future.

That realization led to the creation of the award-winning documentary Daddy Hunger and years of conversations with fathers, mothers, children, educators, counselors, community leaders, and families across the country.

Today, Daddy Hunger is becoming something larger: a mission to help fathers heal, grow, reconnect, and create a healthier legacy for their children.

Our Mission

Every child should feel safe, seen, heard, loved, and prepared.

Daddy Hunger exists to help fathers become more present, emotionally healthy, trustworthy, and prepared so that every child can feel:

Safe.Seen.Heard.Loved.Prepared.

We believe fatherhood is not about perfection.

It is about the willingness to keep becoming.

It is about telling the truth, accepting responsibility, repairing what has been damaged, and choosing not to pass unresolved pain to the next generation.

About Ray Upchurch

Father. Grandfather. Speaker. Filmmaker.

Ray Upchurch is a father, grandfather, speaker, filmmaker, and creator of Daddy Hunger.

His journey into fatherhood did not begin with a perfect example to follow. It began with questions.

What does it mean to become a good father when you did not grow up knowing your own?
How do you protect your children from the wounds, fears, habits, and unfinished parts of your own life?
How do you remain present through divorce, disappointment, financial loss, and personal change?

Ray confronted those questions while raising his two sons. Through success, divorce, the collapse of his business during the financial crisis, therapy, rebuilding, and reconciliation, he learned that providing for children is important—but presence, emotional safety, truth, and love are equally essential.

His sons did not need a perfect father.

They needed a father who was willing to keep becoming.

The Daddy Hunger Journey

Conversations that opened the door to healing.

The original Daddy Hunger documentary brought conversations about fatherhood into communities, universities, museums, youth programs, detention facilities, churches, and public forums.

During those conversations, Ray witnessed the emotional consequences of father absence, father wounds, and unresolved family pain.

He also witnessed something else:

Fathers choosing to reconnect.Children finding language for what they had carried.Families beginning difficult conversations.Men deciding that unhealthy cycles would stop with them.

Those experiences became the foundation for Ray’s forthcoming book, The 10 Commandments of Fatherhood.

The 10 Commandments of Fatherhood

A Message of Redemption, Hope & Love

Book Release · Fall 2026

The 10 Commandments of Fatherhood is a memoir-driven guide to becoming the kind of father whose children feel safe, seen, heard, loved, and prepared.

Drawing from Ray’s childhood, his experience raising two sons, the lessons of divorce and rebuilding, and the stories encountered through Daddy Hunger, the book offers ten principles for healing, responsibility, connection, and legacy.

This is not a book about perfect fathers.

It is a book about fathers who are willing to tell the truth, repair what they can, and keep becoming.

“The greatest gift you will ever give your child is the father you are still becoming.”
Join the Book Launch List

The Five Promises

Five experiences every child deserves.

Safe

A child should feel safe telling the truth, asking for help, admitting a mistake, or sharing fear without humiliation or abandonment.

Seen

A child should know that their father notices who they are—not only what they accomplish.

Heard

A child should feel that their thoughts, emotions, questions, and experiences matter.

Loved

A child should know that love is not something they must earn through performance, agreement, or perfection.

Prepared

A child should receive the wisdom, values, confidence, and practical guidance needed to face life.
